Responsibilities\n//! - Manages interactive PTY sessions (create, reuse, buffer output with caps).\n//! - Uses the shared ToolOrchestrator to handle approval, sandbox selection, and\n//!   retry semantics in a single, descriptive flow.\n//! - Spawns the PTY from a sandbox‑transformed &#96;ExecEnv&#96;; on sandbox denial,\n//!   retries without sandbox when policy allows (no re‑prompt thanks to caching).\n//! - Uses the shared &#96;is_likely_sandbox_denied&#96; heuristic to keep denial messages\n//!   consistent with other exec paths.\n//!\n//! Result&lt;UnifiedExecResponse, UnifiedExecError&gt; {\n        let context =\n            UnifiedExecContext::new(Arc::clone(session), Arc::clone(turn), \"call\".to_string());\n\n        session\n            .services\n            .unified_exec_manager\n            .exec_command(\n                ExecCommandRequest {\n                    command: cmd,\n                    shell: \"/bin/bash\",\n                    login: true,\n                    yield_time_ms,\n                    max_output_tokens: None,\n                },\n                &amp;context,\n            )\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn write_stdin(\n        session: &amp;Arc&lt;Session&gt;,\n        session_id: i32,\n        input: &amp;str,\n        yield_time_ms: Option&lt;u64&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;UnifiedExecResponse, UnifiedExecError&gt; {\n        session\n            .services\n            .unified_exec_manager\n            .write_stdin(WriteStdinRequest {\n                session_id,\n                input,\n                yield_time_ms,\n                max_output_tokens: None,\n            })\n            .await\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn push_chunk_trims_only_excess_bytes() {\n        let mut buffer = OutputBufferState::default();\n        buffer.push_chunk(vec![b'a'; = history.get_rollout_items();\n\n    // Find indices of user message inputs in rollout order.\n    let mut user_positions: Vec&lt;usize&gt; = Vec::new();\n    for (idx, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {\n        if let RolloutItem::ResponseItem(item @ ResponseItem::Message { .. }) = item\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(\n                crate::event_mapping::parse_turn_item(item),\n                Some(TurnItem::UserMessage(_))\n            )\n        {\n            user_positions.push(idx);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // If fewer than or equal to n user messages exist, treat as empty (out of range).\n    if user_positions.len() &lt;= n {\n        return InitialHistory::New;\n    }\n\n    // Cut strictly before the nth user message (do not keep the nth itself).\n    let cut_idx = user_positions[n];\n    let rolled: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items.into_iter().take(cut_idx).collect();\n\n    if rolled.is_empty() {\n        InitialHistory::New\n    } else {\n        InitialHistory::Forked(rolled)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::codex::make_session_and_context;\n    use assert_matches::assert_matches;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ContentItem;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ReasoningItemReasoningSummary;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    fn user_msg(text: &amp;str) -&gt; ResponseItem {\n        ResponseItem::Message {\n            id: None,\n            role: \"user\".to_string(),\n            content: vec![ContentItem::OutputText {\n                text: text.to_string(),\n            }],\n        }\n    }\n    fn assistant_msg(text: &amp;str) -&gt; ResponseItem {\n        ResponseItem::Message {\n            id: None,\n            role: \"assistant\".to_string(),\n            content: vec![ContentItem::OutputText {\n                text: text.to_string(),\n            }],\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn drops_from_last_user_only() {\n        let items = [\n            user_msg(\"u1\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a1\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a2\"),\n            user_msg(\"u2\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a3\"),\n            ResponseItem::Reasoning {\n                id: \"r1\".to_string(),\n                summary: vec![ReasoningItemReasoningSummary::SummaryText {\n                    text: \"s\".to_string(),\n                }],\n                content: None,\n                encrypted_content: None,\n            },\n            ResponseItem::FunctionCall {\n                id: None,\n                name: \"tool\".to_string(),\n                arguments: \"{}\".to_string(),\n                call_id: \"c1\".to_string(),\n            },\n            assistant_msg(\"a4\"),\n        ];\n\n        // Wrap as InitialHistory::Forked with response items only.\n        let initial: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .map(RolloutItem::ResponseItem)\n            .collect();\n        let truncated = truncate_before_nth_user_message(InitialHistory::Forked(initial), 1);\n        let got_items = truncated.get_rollout_items();\n        let expected_items = vec![\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[0].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[1].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[2].clone()),\n        ];\n        assert_eq!(\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;got_items).unwrap(),\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;expected_items).unwrap()\n        );\n\n        let initial2: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = vec![\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[0].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[1].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[2].clone()),\n        ];\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;got_items).unwrap(),\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;expected).unwrap()\n        );\n    }\n}\n",

Self {\n        let auth_manager = crate::AuthManager::from_auth_for_testing(auth);\n        Self {\n            conversations: Arc::new(RwLock::new(HashMap::new())),\n            auth_manager: auth_manager.clone(),\n            session_source: SessionSource::Exec,\n            models_manager: Arc::new(ModelsManager::with_provider(auth_manager, provider)),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn new_conversation(&amp;self, config: Config) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        self.spawn_conversation(config, self.auth_manager.clone())\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn spawn_conversation(\n        &amp;self,\n        config: Config,\n        auth_manager: Arc&lt;AuthManager&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        let CodexSpawnOk {\n            codex,\n            conversation_id,\n        } = Codex::spawn(\n            config,\n            auth_manager,\n            InitialHistory::New,\n            self.session_source.clone(),\n        )\n        .await?;\n        self.finalize_spawn(codex, conversation_id).await\n    }\n\n    async fn finalize_spawn(\n        &amp;self,\n        codex: Codex,\n        conversation_id: ConversationId,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        // The first event must be &#96;SessionInitialized&#96;. Validate and forward it\n        // to the caller so that they can display it in the conversation\n        // history.\n        let event = codex.next_event().await?;\n        let session_configured = match event {\n            Event {\n                id,\n                msg: EventMsg::SessionConfigured(session_configured),\n            } if id == INITIAL_SUBMIT_ID =&gt; session_configured,\n            _ =&gt; {\n                return Err(CodexErr::SessionConfiguredNotFirstEvent);\n            }\n        };\n\n        let conversation = Arc::new(CodexConversation::new(\n            codex,\n            session_configured.rollout_path.clone(),\n        ));\n        self.conversations\n            .write()\n            .await\n            .insert(conversation_id, conversation.clone());\n\n        Ok(NewConversation {\n            conversation_id,\n            conversation,\n            session_configured,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub async fn get_conversation(\n        &amp;self,\n        conversation_id: ConversationId,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;Arc&lt;CodexConversation&gt;&gt; {\n        let conversations = self.conversations.read().await;\n        conversations\n            .get(&amp;conversation_id)\n            .cloned()\n            .ok_or_else(|| CodexErr::ConversationNotFound(conversation_id))\n    }\n\n    pub async fn resume_conversation_from_rollout(\n        &amp;self,\n        config: Config,\n        rollout_path: PathBuf,\n        auth_manager: Arc&lt;AuthManager&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        let initial_history = RolloutRecorder::get_rollout_history(&amp;rollout_path).await?;\n        self.resume_conversation_with_history(config, initial_history, auth_manager)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    pub async fn resume_conversation_with_history(\n        &amp;self,\n        config: Config,\n        initial_history: InitialHistory,\n        auth_manager: Arc&lt;AuthManager&gt;,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        let CodexSpawnOk {\n            codex,\n            conversation_id,\n        } = Codex::spawn(\n            config,\n            auth_manager,\n            initial_history,\n            self.session_source.clone(),\n        )\n        .await?;\n        self.finalize_spawn(codex, conversation_id).await\n    }\n\n    /// Removes the conversation from the manager's internal map, though the\n    /// conversation is stored as &#96;Arc&lt;CodexConversation&gt;&#96;, it is possible that\n    /// other references to it exist elsewhere. Returns the conversation if the\n    /// conversation was found and removed.\n    pub async fn remove_conversation(\n        &amp;self,\n        conversation_id: &amp;ConversationId,\n    ) -&gt; Option&lt;Arc&lt;CodexConversation&gt;&gt; {\n        self.conversations.write().await.remove(conversation_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Fork an existing conversation by taking messages up to the given position\n    /// (not including the message at the given position) and starting a new\n    /// conversation with identical configuration (unless overridden by the\n    /// caller's &#96;config&#96;). The new conversation will have a fresh id.\n    pub async fn fork_conversation(\n        &amp;self,\n        nth_user_message: usize,\n        config: Config,\n        path: PathBuf,\n    ) -&gt; CodexResult&lt;NewConversation&gt; {\n        // Compute the prefix up to the cut point.\n        let history = RolloutRecorder::get_rollout_history(&amp;path).await?;\n        let history = truncate_before_nth_user_message(history, nth_user_message);\n\n        // Spawn a new conversation with the computed initial history.\n        let auth_manager = self.auth_manager.clone();\n        let CodexSpawnOk {\n            codex,\n            conversation_id,\n        } = Codex::spawn(config, auth_manager, history, self.session_source.clone()).await?;\n\n        self.finalize_spawn(codex, conversation_id).await\n    }\n}\n\n/// Return a prefix of &#96;items&#96; obtained by cutting strictly before the nth user message\n/// (0-based) and all items that follow it.\nfn truncate_before_nth_user_message(history: InitialHistory, n: usize) -&gt; InitialHistory {\n    // Work directly on rollout items, and cut the vector at the nth user message input.\n    let items: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = history.get_rollout_items();\n\n    // Find indices of user message inputs in rollout order.\n    let mut user_positions: Vec&lt;usize&gt; = Vec::new();\n    for (idx, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {\n        if let RolloutItem::ResponseItem(item @ ResponseItem::Message { .. }) = item\n            &amp;&amp; matches!(\n                crate::event_mapping::parse_turn_item(item),\n                Some(TurnItem::UserMessage(_))\n            )\n        {\n            user_positions.push(idx);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // If fewer than or equal to n user messages exist, treat as empty (out of range).\n    if user_positions.len() &lt;= n {\n        return InitialHistory::New;\n    }\n\n    // Cut strictly before the nth user message (do not keep the nth itself).\n    let cut_idx = user_positions[n];\n    let rolled: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items.into_iter().take(cut_idx).collect();\n\n    if rolled.is_empty() {\n        InitialHistory::New\n    } else {\n        InitialHistory::Forked(rolled)\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::codex::make_session_and_context;\n    use assert_matches::assert_matches;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ContentItem;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ReasoningItemReasoningSummary;\n    use codex_protocol::models::ResponseItem;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    fn user_msg(text: &amp;str) -&gt; ResponseItem {\n        ResponseItem::Message {\n            id: None,\n            role: \"user\".to_string(),\n            content: vec![ContentItem::OutputText {\n                text: text.to_string(),\n            }],\n        }\n    }\n    fn assistant_msg(text: &amp;str) -&gt; ResponseItem {\n        ResponseItem::Message {\n            id: None,\n            role: \"assistant\".to_string(),\n            content: vec![ContentItem::OutputText {\n                text: text.to_string(),\n            }],\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn drops_from_last_user_only() {\n        let items = [\n            user_msg(\"u1\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a1\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a2\"),\n            user_msg(\"u2\"),\n            assistant_msg(\"a3\"),\n            ResponseItem::Reasoning {\n                id: \"r1\".to_string(),\n                summary: vec![ReasoningItemReasoningSummary::SummaryText {\n                    text: \"s\".to_string(),\n                }],\n                content: None,\n                encrypted_content: None,\n            },\n            ResponseItem::FunctionCall {\n                id: None,\n                name: \"tool\".to_string(),\n                arguments: \"{}\".to_string(),\n                call_id: \"c1\".to_string(),\n            },\n            assistant_msg(\"a4\"),\n        ];\n\n        // Wrap as InitialHistory::Forked with response items only.\n        let initial: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .map(RolloutItem::ResponseItem)\n            .collect();\n        let truncated = truncate_before_nth_user_message(InitialHistory::Forked(initial), 1);\n        let got_items = truncated.get_rollout_items();\n        let expected_items = vec![\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[0].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[1].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[2].clone()),\n        ];\n        assert_eq!(\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;got_items).unwrap(),\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;expected_items).unwrap()\n        );\n\n        let initial2: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .map(RolloutItem::ResponseItem)\n            .collect();\n        let truncated2 = truncate_before_nth_user_message(InitialHistory::Forked(initial2), 2);\n        assert_matches!(truncated2, InitialHistory::New);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn ignores_session_prefix_messages_when_truncating() {\n        let (session, turn_context) = make_session_and_context();\n        let mut items = session.build_initial_context(&amp;turn_context);\n        items.push(user_msg(\"feature request\"));\n        items.push(assistant_msg(\"ack\"));\n        items.push(user_msg(\"second question\"));\n        items.push(assistant_msg(\"answer\"));\n\n        let rollout_items: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = items\n            .iter()\n            .cloned()\n            .map(RolloutItem::ResponseItem)\n            .collect();\n\n        let truncated = truncate_before_nth_user_message(InitialHistory::Forked(rollout_items), 1);\n        let got_items = truncated.get_rollout_items();\n\n        let expected: Vec&lt;RolloutItem&gt; = vec![\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[0].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[1].clone()),\n            RolloutItem::ResponseItem(items[2].clone()),\n        ];\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;got_items).unwrap(),\n            serde_json::to_value(&amp;expected).unwrap()\n        );\n    }\n}\n"
}

Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    use regex::Regex;\n\n    // Pattern 1: \"- language: ja\" (list format)\n    // Pattern 2: \"language: en\" (key-value format)\n    let patterns = [\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*review_language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n    ];\n\n    for pattern_str in &amp;patterns {\n        if let Ok(re) = Regex::new(pattern_str) {\n            if let Some(captures) = re.captures(content) {\n                if let Some(lang_match) = captures.get(1) {\n                    let lang = lang_match.as_str().to_lowercase();\n                    tracing::debug!(\"Extracted language setting: {}\", lang);\n                    return Some(lang);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    None\n}\n\n/// Get language setting from project documentation\npub async fn get_language_setting(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; Unexpected I/O failures bubble up as &#96;Err&#96; so\n/// callers can decide how to handle them.\npub async fn read_project_docs(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;Option&lt;String&gt;&gt; {\n    let max_total = config.project_doc_max_bytes;\n\n    if max_total == 0 {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let paths = discover_project_doc_paths(config)?;\n    if paths.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let mut remaining: u64 = max_total as u64;\n    let mut parts: Vec&lt;String&gt; = Vec::new();\n\n    for p in paths {\n        if remaining == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        let file = match tokio::fs::File::open(&amp;p).await {\n            Ok(f) =&gt; f,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound =&gt; continue,\n            Err(e) =&gt; return Err(e),\n        };\n\n        let size = file.metadata().await?.len();\n        let mut reader = tokio::io::BufReader::new(file).take(remaining);\n        let mut data: Vec&lt;u8&gt; = Vec::new();\n        reader.read_to_end(&amp;mut data).await?;\n\n        if size &gt; remaining {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                \"Project doc &#96;{}&#96; exceeds remaining budget ({} bytes) - truncating.\",\n                p.display(),\n                remaining,\n            );\n        }\n\n        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&amp;data).to_string();\n        if !text.trim().is_empty() {\n            parts.push(text);\n            remaining = remaining.saturating_sub(data.len() as u64);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if parts.is_empty() {\n        Ok(None)\n    } else {\n        Ok(Some(parts.join(\"\\n\\n\")))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Discover the list of AGENTS.md files using the same search rules as\n/// &#96;read_project_docs&#96;, but return the file paths instead of concatenated\n/// contents. We do **not** walk past the Git root.\n\nuse crate::config::Config;\nuse crate::features::Feature;\nuse crate::skills::SkillMetadata;\nuse crate::skills::render_skills_section;\nuse dunce::canonicalize as normalize_path;\nuse std::path::PathBuf;\nuse tokio::io::AsyncReadExt;\nuse tracing::error;\n\n/// Default filename scanned for project-level docs.\npub const DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME: &amp;str = \"AGENTS.md\";\n/// Preferred local override for project-level docs.\npub const LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME: &amp;str = \"AGENTS.override.md\";\n\n/// When both &#96;Config::instructions&#96; and &#96;AGENTS.md&#96; (if present) into a single\n/// string of instructions.\npub(crate) async fn get_user_instructions(\n    config: &amp;Config,\n    skills: Option&lt;&amp;[SkillMetadata]&gt;,\n) -&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    let skills_section = if config.features.enabled(Feature::Skills) {\n        skills.and_then(render_skills_section)\n    } else {\n        None\n    };\n\n    let project_docs = match read_project_docs(config).await {\n        Ok(docs) =&gt; Some(format!(\"{existing}{PROJECT_DOC_SEPARATOR}{project_doc}\")),\n            None =&gt; Some(project_doc),\n        };\n    }\n\n    if let Some(skills_section) = skills_section {\n        out = match out {\n            Some(existing) =&gt; Option&lt;String&gt; {\n    use regex::Regex;\n\n    // Pattern 1: \"- language: ja\" (list format)\n    // Pattern 2: \"language: en\" (key-value format)\n    let patterns = [\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n        r\"(?mi)^-?\\s*review_language:\\s*(\\w+)\",\n    ];\n\n    for pattern_str in &amp;patterns {\n        if let Ok(re) = Regex::new(pattern_str) {\n            if let Some(captures) = re.captures(content) {\n                if let Some(lang_match) = captures.get(1) {\n                    let lang = lang_match.as_str().to_lowercase();\n                    tracing::debug!(\"Extracted language setting: {}\", lang);\n                    return Some(lang);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    None\n}\n\n/// Get language setting from project documentation\npub async fn get_language_setting(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; Unexpected I/O failures bubble up as &#96;Err&#96; so\n/// callers can decide how to handle them.\npub async fn read_project_docs(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;Option&lt;String&gt;&gt; {\n    let max_total = config.project_doc_max_bytes;\n\n    if max_total == 0 {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let paths = discover_project_doc_paths(config)?;\n    if paths.is_empty() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n\n    let mut remaining: u64 = max_total as u64;\n    let mut parts: Vec&lt;String&gt; = Vec::new();\n\n    for p in paths {\n        if remaining == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        let file = match tokio::fs::File::open(&amp;p).await {\n            Ok(f) =&gt; f,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound =&gt; continue,\n            Err(e) =&gt; return Err(e),\n        };\n\n        let size = file.metadata().await?.len();\n        let mut reader = tokio::io::BufReader::new(file).take(remaining);\n        let mut data: Vec&lt;u8&gt; = Vec::new();\n        reader.read_to_end(&amp;mut data).await?;\n\n        if size &gt; remaining {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                \"Project doc &#96;{}&#96; exceeds remaining budget ({} bytes) - truncating.\",\n                p.display(),\n                remaining,\n            );\n        }\n\n        let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&amp;data).to_string();\n        if !text.trim().is_empty() {\n            parts.push(text);\n            remaining = remaining.saturating_sub(data.len() as u64);\n        }\n    }\n\n    if parts.is_empty() {\n        Ok(None)\n    } else {\n        Ok(Some(parts.join(\"\\n\\n\")))\n    }\n}\n\n/// Discover the list of AGENTS.md files using the same search rules as\n/// &#96;read_project_docs&#96;, but return the file paths instead of concatenated\n/// contents. The list is ordered from repository root to the current working\n/// directory (inclusive). Symlinks are allowed. When &#96;project_doc_max_bytes&#96;\n/// is zero, returns an empty list.\npub fn discover_project_doc_paths(config: &amp;Config) -&gt; std::io::Result&lt;Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt;&gt; {\n    let mut dir = config.cwd.clone();\n    if let Ok(canon) = normalize_path(&amp;dir) {\n        dir = canon;\n    }\n\n    // Build chain from cwd upwards and detect git root.\n    let mut chain: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt; = vec![dir.clone()];\n    let mut git_root: Option&lt;PathBuf&gt; = None;\n    let mut cursor = dir;\n    while let Some(parent) = cursor.parent() {\n        let git_marker = cursor.join(\".git\");\n        let git_exists = match std::fs::metadata(&amp;git_marker) {\n            Ok(_) =&gt; true,\n            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound =&gt; false,\n            Err(e) =&gt; return Err(e),\n        };\n\n        if git_exists {\n            git_root = Some(cursor.clone());\n            break;\n        }\n\n        chain.push(parent.to_path_buf());\n        cursor = parent.to_path_buf();\n    }\n\n    let search_dirs: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt; = if let Some(root) = git_root {\n        let mut dirs: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt; = Vec::new();\n        let mut saw_root = false;\n        for p in chain.iter().rev() {\n            if !saw_root {\n                if p == &amp;root {\n                    saw_root = true;\n                } else {\n                    continue;\n                }\n            }\n            dirs.push(p.clone());\n        }\n        dirs\n    } else {\n        vec![config.cwd.clone()]\n    };\n\n    let mut found: Vec&lt;PathBuf&gt; = Vec::new();\n    let candidate_filenames = candidate_filenames(config);\n    for d in search_dirs {\n        for name in &amp;candidate_filenames {\n            let candidate = d.join(name);\n            match std::fs::symlink_metadata(&amp;candidate) {\n                Ok(md) =&gt; {\n                    let ft = md.file_type();\n                    // Allow regular files and symlinks; opening will later fail for dangling links.\n                    if ft.is_file() || ft.is_symlink() {\n                        found.push(candidate);\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound =&gt; continue,\n                Err(e) =&gt; return Err(e),\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    Ok(found)\n}\n\nfn candidate_filenames&lt;'a&gt;(config: &amp;'a Config) -&gt; Vec&lt;&amp;'a str&gt; {\n    let mut names: Vec&lt;&amp;'a str&gt; =\n        Vec::with_capacity(2 + config.project_doc_fallback_filenames.len());\n    names.push(LOCAL_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME);\n    names.push(DEFAULT_PROJECT_DOC_FILENAME);\n    for candidate in &amp;config.project_doc_fallback_filenames {\n        let candidate = candidate.as_str();\n        if candidate.is_empty() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        if !names.contains(&amp;candidate) {\n            names.push(candidate);\n        }\n    }\n    names\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use crate::config::ConfigOverrides;\n    use crate::config::ConfigToml;\n    use crate::skills::load_skills;\n    use std::fs;\n    use tempfile::TempDir;\n\n    /// Helper that returns a &#96;Config&#96; pointing at &#96;root&#96; and using &#96;limit&#96; as\n    /// the maximum number of bytes to embed from AGENTS.md. The caller can\n    /// optionally specify a custom &#96;instructions&#96; string – when &#96;None&#96; the\n    /// value is cleared to mimic a scenario where no system instructions have\n    /// been configured.\n    fn make_config(root: &amp;TempDir, limit: usize, instructions: Option&lt;&amp;str&gt;) -&gt; Config {\n        let codex_home = TempDir::new().unwrap();\n        let mut config = Config::load_from_base_config_with_overrides(\n            ConfigToml::default(),\n            ConfigOverrides::default(),\n            codex_home.path().to_path_buf(),\n        )\n        .expect(\"defaults for test should always succeed\");\n\n        config.cwd = root.path().to_path_buf();\n        config.project_doc_max_bytes = limit;\n\n        config.user_instructions = instructions.map(ToOwned::to_owned);\n        config\n    }\n\n    fn make_config_with_fallback(\n        root: &amp;TempDir,\n        limit: usize,\n        instructions: Option&lt;&amp;str&gt;,\n        fallbacks: &amp;[&amp;str],\n    ) -&gt; Config {\n        let mut config = make_config(root, limit, instructions);\n        config.project_doc_fallback_filenames = fallbacks\n            .iter()\n            .map(std::string::ToString::to_string)\n            .collect();\n        config\n    }\n\n    /// AGENTS.md missing – should yield &#96;None&#96;.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn no_doc_file_returns_none() {\n        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"tempdir\");\n\n        let res = get_user_instructions(&amp;make_config(&amp;tmp, 4096, None), None).await;\n        assert!(\n            res.is_none(),\n            \"Expected None when AGENTS.md is absent and no system instructions provided\"\n        );\n        assert!(res.is_none(), \"Expected None when AGENTS.md is absent\");\n    }\n\n    /// Small file within the byte-limit is returned unmodified.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn doc_smaller_than_limit_is_returned() {\n        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"tempdir\");\n        fs::write(tmp.path().join(\"AGENTS.md\"), \"hello world\").unwrap();\n\n        let res = get_user_instructions(&amp;make_config(&amp;tmp, 4096, None), None)\n            .await\n            .expect(\"doc expected\");\n\n        assert_eq!(\n            res, \"hello world\",\n            \"The document should be returned verbatim when it is smaller than the limit and there are no existing instructions\"\n        );\n    }\n\n    /// Oversize file is truncated to &#96;project_doc_max_bytes&#96;.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn doc_larger_than_limit_is_truncated() {\n        const LIMIT: usize = 1024;\n        let tmp = tempfile::tempdir().expect(\"tempdir\");\n\n        let huge = \"A\".repeat(LIMIT * 2); let nested = repo.path().join(\"workspace/crate_a\");\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&amp;nested).unwrap();\n\n        // Build config pointing at the nested dir.\n        let mut cfg = assert_eq!(res, \"root level doc\");\n    }\n\n    /// Explicitly setting the byte-limit to zero disables project docs.\n    #[tokio::test]\n    async fn zero_byte_limit_disables_docs() {\n        let Self {\n        Self {\n            sandbox: SandboxManager::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub async fn run&lt;Rq, Out, T&gt;(\n        &amp;mut self,\n        tool: &amp;mut T,\n        req: &amp;Rq,\n        tool_ctx: &amp;ToolCtx&lt;'_&gt;,\n        turn_ctx: &amp;crate::codex::TurnContext,\n        approval_policy: AskForApproval,\n    ) -&gt; Result&lt;Out, ToolError&gt;\n    where\n        T: ToolRuntime&lt;Rq, Out&gt;,\n    {\n        let otel = turn_ctx.client.get_otel_event_manager();\n        let otel_tn = &amp;tool_ctx.tool_name;\n        let otel_ci = &amp;tool_ctx.call_id;\n        let otel_user = codex_otel::otel_event_manager::ToolDecisionSource::User;\n        let otel_cfg = codex_otel::otel_event_manager::ToolDecisionSource::Config;\n\n        // 1) Approval\n        let needs_initial_approval =\n            tool.wants_initial_approval(req, approval_policy, &amp;turn_ctx.sandbox_policy);\n        let mut already_approved = false;\n\n        if needs_initial_approval {\n            let approval_ctx = ApprovalCtx {\n                session: tool_ctx.session,\n                turn: turn_ctx,\n                call_id: &amp;tool_ctx.call_id,\n                retry_reason: None,\n            };\n            let decision = tool.start_approval_async(req, approval_ctx).await;\n\n            otel.tool_decision(otel_tn, otel_ci, decision.clone(), otel_user.clone());\n\n            match decision {\n                ReviewDecision::Denied | ReviewDecision::Abort =&gt; {\n                    return Err(ToolError::Rejected(\"rejected by user\".to_string()));\n                }\n                ReviewDecision::Approved | ReviewDecision::ApprovedForSession =&gt; {}\n            }\n            already_approved = true;\n        } else {\n            otel.tool_decision(otel_tn, otel_ci, ReviewDecision::Approved, otel_cfg);\n        }\n\n        // 2) First attempt under the selected sandbox.\n        let mut initial_sandbox = self\n            .sandbox\n            .select_initial(&amp;turn_ctx.sandbox_policy, tool.sandbox_preference());\n        if tool.wants_escalated_first_attempt(req) {\n            initial_sandbox = crate::exec::SandboxType::None;\n        }\n        // Platform-specific flag gating is handled by SandboxManager::select_initial\n        // via crate::safety::get_platform_sandbox().\n        let initial_attempt = SandboxAttempt {\n            sandbox: initial_sandbox,\n            policy: &amp;turn_ctx.sandbox_policy,\n            manager: &amp;self.sandbox,\n            sandbox_cwd: &amp;turn_ctx.cwd,\n            codex_linux_sandbox_exe: turn_ctx.codex_linux_sandbox_exe.as_ref(),\n        };\n\n        match tool.run(req, &amp;initial_attempt, tool_ctx).await {\n            Ok(out) =&gt; {\n                // We have a successful initial result\n                Ok(out)\n            }\n            Err(ToolError::Codex(CodexErr::Sandbox(SandboxErr::Denied { output }))) =&gt; {\n                if !tool.escalate_on_failure() {\n                    return Err(ToolError::Codex(CodexErr::Sandbox(SandboxErr::Denied {\n                        output,\n                    })));\n                }\n                // Under &#96;Never&#96; or &#96;OnRequest&#96;, do not retry without sandbox; surface a concise\n                // sandbox denial that preserves the original output.\n                if !tool.wants_no_sandbox_approval(approval_policy) {\n                    return Err(ToolError::Codex(CodexErr::Sandbox(SandboxErr::Denied {\n                        output,\n                    })));\n                }\n\n                // Ask for approval before retrying without sandbox.\n                if !tool.should_bypass_approval(approval_policy, already_approved) {\n                    let reason_msg = build_denial_reason_from_output(output.as_ref());\n                    let approval_ctx = ApprovalCtx {\n                        session: tool_ctx.session,\n                        turn: turn_ctx,\n                        call_id: &amp;tool_ctx.call_id,\n                        retry_reason: Some(reason_msg),\n                    };\n\n                    let decision = tool.start_approval_async(req, approval_ctx).await;\n                    otel.tool_decision(otel_tn, otel_ci, decision.clone(), otel_user);\n\n                    match decision {\n                        ReviewDecision::Denied | ReviewDecision::Abort =&gt; {\n                            return Err(ToolError::Rejected(\"rejected by user\".to_string()));\n                        }\n                        ReviewDecision::Approved | ReviewDecision::ApprovedForSession =&gt; {}\n                    }\n                }\n\n                let escalated_attempt = SandboxAttempt {\n                    sandbox: crate::exec::SandboxType::None,\n                    policy: &amp;turn_ctx.sandbox_policy,\n                    manager: &amp;self.sandbox,\n                    sandbox_cwd: &amp;turn_ctx.cwd,\n                    codex_linux_sandbox_exe: None,\n                };\n\n                // Second attempt.\n                (*tool).run(req, &amp;escalated_attempt, tool_ctx).await\n            }\n            other =&gt; other,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn build_denial_reason_from_output(_output: &amp;ExecToolCallOutput) -&gt; String {\n    // Keep approval reason terse and stable for UX/tests, but accept the\n    // output so we can evolve heuristics later without touching call sites.\n    \"command failed; retry without sandbox?\".to_string()\n}\n",

Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"read_mcp_resource\".to_string(),\n        description:\n            \"Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.\"\n                .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"server\".to_string(), \"uri\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n/// TODO(dylan): deprecate once we get rid of json tool\n#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub(crate) struct ApplyPatchToolArgs {\n    pub(crate) input: String,\n}\n\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Responses API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=responses\npub fn create_tools_json_for_responses_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    let mut tools_json = Vec::new();\n\n    for tool in tools {\n        let json = serde_json::to_value(tool)?;\n        tools_json.push(json);\n    }\n\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Chat Completions API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=chat\npub(crate) fn create_tools_json_for_chat_completions_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    // We start with the JSON for the Responses API and than rewrite it to match\n    // the chat completions tool call format.\n    let responses_api_tools_json = create_tools_json_for_responses_api(tools)?;\n    let tools_json = responses_api_tools_json\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|mut tool| {\n            if tool.get(\"type\") != Some(&amp;serde_json::Value::String(\"function\".to_string())) {\n                return None;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(map) = tool.as_object_mut() {\n                let name = map\n                    .get(\"name\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .unwrap_or_default()\n                    .to_string();\n                // Remove \"type\" field as it is not needed in chat completions.\n                map.remove(\"type\");\n                Some(json!({\n                    \"type\": \"function\",\n                    \"name\": name,\n                    \"function\": map,\n                }))\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect::&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt;();\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n\npub(crate) fn mcp_tool_to_openai_tool(\n    fully_qualified_name: String,\n    tool: mcp_types::Tool,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;ResponsesApiTool, serde_json::Error&gt; {\n    let mcp_types::Tool {\n        description,\n        mut input_schema,\n        ..\n    } = tool;\n\n    // OpenAI models mandate the \"properties\" field in the schema. The Agents\n    // SDK fixed this by inserting an empty object for \"properties\" if it is not\n    // already present https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/449\n    // so here we do the same.\n    if input_schema.properties.is_none() {\n        input_schema.properties = Some(serde_json::Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()));\n    }\n\n    // Serialize to a raw JSON value so we can sanitize schemas coming from MCP\n    // servers. Some servers omit the top-level or nested &#96;type&#96; in JSON\n    // Schemas (e.g. using enum/anyOf), or use unsupported variants like\n    // &#96;integer&#96;. Our internal JsonSchema is a small subset and requires\n    // &#96;type&#96;, so we coerce/sanitize here for compatibility.\n    let mut serialized_input_schema = serde_json::to_value(input_schema)?;\n    sanitize_json_schema(&amp;mut serialized_input_schema);\n    let input_schema = serde_json::from_value::&lt;JsonSchema&gt;(serialized_input_schema)?;\n\n    Ok(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: fully_qualified_name,\n        description: description.unwrap_or_default(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: input_schema,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a JSON Schema (as serde_json::Value) so it can fit our limited\n/// JsonSchema enum. This function:\n/// - Ensures every schema object has a \"type\". If missing, infers it from\n///   common keywords (properties =&gt; object, items =&gt; array, enum/const/format =&gt; string)\n///   and otherwise defaults to \"string\".\n/// - Fills required child fields (e.g. array items, object properties) with\n///   permissive defaults when absent.\nfn sanitize_json_schema(value: &amp;mut JsonValue) {\n    match value {\n        JsonValue::Bool(_) =&gt; {\n            // JSON Schema boolean form: true/false. Coerce to an accept-all string.\n            *value = json!({ \"type\": \"string\" });\n        }\n        JsonValue::Array(arr) =&gt; {\n            for v in arr.iter_mut() {\n                sanitize_json_schema(v);\n            }\n        }\n        JsonValue::Object(map) =&gt; {\n            // First, recursively sanitize known nested schema holders\n            if let Some(props) = map.get_mut(\"properties\")\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(props_map) = props.as_object_mut()\n            {\n                for (_k, v) in props_map.iter_mut() {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(items) = map.get_mut(\"items\") {\n                sanitize_json_schema(items);\n            }\n            // Some schemas use oneOf/anyOf/allOf - sanitize their entries\n            for combiner in [\"oneOf\", \"anyOf\", \"allOf\", \"prefixItems\"] {\n                if let Some(v) = map.get_mut(combiner) {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Normalize/ensure type\n            let mut ty = map.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(str::to_string);\n\n            // If type is an array (union), pick first supported; else leave to inference\n            if ty.is_none()\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(JsonValue::Array(types)) = map.get(\"type\")\n            {\n                for t in types {\n                    if let Some(tt) = t.as_str()\n                        &amp;&amp; matches!(\n                            tt,\n                            \"object\" | \"array\" | \"string\" | \"number\" | \"integer\" | \"boolean\"\n                        )\n                    {\n                        ty = Some(tt.to_string());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Infer type if still missing\n            if ty.is_none() {\n                if map.contains_key(\"properties\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"required\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"additionalProperties\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"object\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"items\") || map.contains_key(\"prefixItems\") {\n                    ty = Some(\"array\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"enum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"const\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"format\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"string\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"minimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"maximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMinimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMaximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"multipleOf\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"number\".to_string());\n                }\n            }\n            // If we still couldn't infer, default to string\n            let ty = ty.unwrap_or_else(|| \"string\".to_string());\n            map.insert(\"type\".to_string(), JsonValue::String(ty.to_string()));\n\n            // Ensure object schemas have properties map\n            if ty == \"object\" {\n                if !map.contains_key(\"properties\") {\n                    map.insert(\n                        \"properties\".to_string(),\n                        JsonValue::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),\n                    );\n                }\n                // If additionalProperties is an object schema, sanitize it too.\n                // Leave booleans as-is, since JSON Schema allows boolean here.\n                if let Some(ap) = map.get_mut(\"additionalProperties\") {\n                    let is_bool = matches!(ap, JsonValue::Bool(_));\n                    if !is_bool {\n                        sanitize_json_schema(ap);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Ensure array schemas have items\n            if ty == \"array\" &amp;&amp; !map.contains_key(\"items\") {\n                map.insert(\"items\".to_string(), json!({ \"type\": \"string\" }));\n            }\n        }\n        _ =&gt; {}\n    }\n}\n\n/// Builds the tool registry builder while collecting tool specs for later serialization.\npub(crate) fn build_specs(\n    config: &amp;ToolsConfig,\n    mcp_tools: Option&lt;HashMap&lt;String, Defaults to the session's working directory.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"limit\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Maximum number of file paths to return (defaults to 100).\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"grep_files\".to_string(),\n        description: \"Finds files whose contents match the pattern and lists them by modification \\\n                      time.\"\n            .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"pattern\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n\npub(crate) fn create_read_file_tool() -&gt; ToolSpec {\n    let mut properties = BTreeMap::new();\n    properties.insert(\n        \"file_path\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\"Absolute path to the file\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"offset\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"The line number to start reading from. Must be 1 or greater.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"limit\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\"The maximum number of lines to return.\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"mode\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Optional mode selector: \\\"slice\\\" for simple ranges (default) or \\\"indentation\\\" \\\n                 to expand around an anchor line.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    let mut indentation_properties = BTreeMap::new();\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"anchor_line\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Anchor line to center the indentation lookup on (defaults to offset).\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n     ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"include_siblings\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Boolean {\n            description: Some(\n                \"When true, include additional blocks that share the anchor indentation.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"include_header\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Boolean {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Include doc comments or attributes directly above the selected block.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    indentation_properties.insert(\n        \"max_lines\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Hard cap on Must be 1 or greater.\".to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"limit\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\"The maximum number of entries to return.\".to_string()),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"depth\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::Number {\n            description: Some(\n                \"The maximum directory depth to traverse. When omitted, lists resources from every configured server.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"cursor\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Opaque cursor returned by a previous list_mcp_resources call for the same server.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"list_mcp_resources\".to_string(),\n        description: \"Lists resources provided by MCP servers. Must match the 'server' field returned by list_mcp_resources.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n    properties.insert(\n        \"uri\".to_string(),\n        JsonSchema::String {\n            description: Some(\n                \"Resource URI to read. Must be one of the URIs returned by list_mcp_resources.\"\n                    .to_string(),\n            ),\n        },\n    );\n\n    ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: \"read_mcp_resource\".to_string(),\n        description:\n            \"Read a specific resource from an MCP server given the server name and resource URI.\"\n                .to_string(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: JsonSchema::Object {\n            properties,\n            required: Some(vec![\"server\".to_string(), \"uri\".to_string()]),\n            additional_properties: Some(false.into()),\n        },\n    })\n}\n/// TODO(dylan): deprecate once we get rid of json tool\n#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub(crate) struct ApplyPatchToolArgs {\n    pub(crate) input: String,\n}\n\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Responses API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=responses\npub fn create_tools_json_for_responses_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    let mut tools_json = Vec::new();\n\n    for tool in tools {\n        let json = serde_json::to_value(tool)?;\n        tools_json.push(json);\n    }\n\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n/// Returns JSON values that are compatible with Function Calling in the\n/// Chat Completions API:\n/// https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling?api-mode=chat\npub(crate) fn create_tools_json_for_chat_completions_api(\n    tools: &amp;[ToolSpec],\n) -&gt; crate::error::Result&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt; {\n    // We start with the JSON for the Responses API and than rewrite it to match\n    // the chat completions tool call format.\n    let responses_api_tools_json = create_tools_json_for_responses_api(tools)?;\n    let tools_json = responses_api_tools_json\n        .into_iter()\n        .filter_map(|mut tool| {\n            if tool.get(\"type\") != Some(&amp;serde_json::Value::String(\"function\".to_string())) {\n                return None;\n            }\n\n            if let Some(map) = tool.as_object_mut() {\n                let name = map\n                    .get(\"name\")\n                    .and_then(|v| v.as_str())\n                    .unwrap_or_default()\n                    .to_string();\n                // Remove \"type\" field as it is not needed in chat completions.\n                map.remove(\"type\");\n                Some(json!({\n                    \"type\": \"function\",\n                    \"name\": name,\n                    \"function\": map,\n                }))\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .collect::&lt;Vec&lt;serde_json::Value&gt;&gt;();\n    Ok(tools_json)\n}\n\npub(crate) fn mcp_tool_to_openai_tool(\n    fully_qualified_name: String,\n    tool: mcp_types::Tool,\n) -&gt; Result&lt;ResponsesApiTool, serde_json::Error&gt; {\n    let mcp_types::Tool {\n        description,\n        mut input_schema,\n        ..\n    } = tool;\n\n    // OpenAI models mandate the \"properties\" field in the schema. The Agents\n    // SDK fixed this by inserting an empty object for \"properties\" if it is not\n    // already present https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/449\n    // so here we do the same.\n    if input_schema.properties.is_none() {\n        input_schema.properties = Some(serde_json::Value::Object(serde_json::Map::new()));\n    }\n\n    // Serialize to a raw JSON value so we can sanitize schemas coming from MCP\n    // servers. Some servers omit the top-level or nested &#96;type&#96; in JSON\n    // Schemas (e.g. using enum/anyOf), or use unsupported variants like\n    // &#96;integer&#96;. Our internal JsonSchema is a small subset and requires\n    // &#96;type&#96;, so we coerce/sanitize here for compatibility.\n    let mut serialized_input_schema = serde_json::to_value(input_schema)?;\n    sanitize_json_schema(&amp;mut serialized_input_schema);\n    let input_schema = serde_json::from_value::&lt;JsonSchema&gt;(serialized_input_schema)?;\n\n    Ok(ResponsesApiTool {\n        name: fully_qualified_name,\n        description: description.unwrap_or_default(),\n        strict: false,\n        parameters: input_schema,\n    })\n}\n\n/// Sanitize a JSON Schema (as serde_json::Value) so it can fit our limited\n/// JsonSchema enum. This function:\n/// - Ensures every schema object has a \"type\". If missing, infers it from\n///   common keywords (properties =&gt; object, items =&gt; array, enum/const/format =&gt; string)\n///   and otherwise defaults to \"string\".\n/// - Fills required child fields (e.g. array items, object properties) with\n///   permissive defaults when absent.\nfn sanitize_json_schema(value: &amp;mut JsonValue) {\n    match value {\n        JsonValue::Bool(_) =&gt; {\n            // JSON Schema boolean form: true/false. Coerce to an accept-all string.\n            *value = json!({ \"type\": \"string\" });\n        }\n        JsonValue::Array(arr) =&gt; {\n            for v in arr.iter_mut() {\n                sanitize_json_schema(v);\n            }\n        }\n        JsonValue::Object(map) =&gt; {\n            // First, recursively sanitize known nested schema holders\n            if let Some(props) = map.get_mut(\"properties\")\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(props_map) = props.as_object_mut()\n            {\n                for (_k, v) in props_map.iter_mut() {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(items) = map.get_mut(\"items\") {\n                sanitize_json_schema(items);\n            }\n            // Some schemas use oneOf/anyOf/allOf - sanitize their entries\n            for combiner in [\"oneOf\", \"anyOf\", \"allOf\", \"prefixItems\"] {\n                if let Some(v) = map.get_mut(combiner) {\n                    sanitize_json_schema(v);\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Normalize/ensure type\n            let mut ty = map.get(\"type\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(str::to_string);\n\n            // If type is an array (union), pick first supported; else leave to inference\n            if ty.is_none()\n                &amp;&amp; let Some(JsonValue::Array(types)) = map.get(\"type\")\n            {\n                for t in types {\n                    if let Some(tt) = t.as_str()\n                        &amp;&amp; matches!(\n                            tt,\n                            \"object\" | \"array\" | \"string\" | \"number\" | \"integer\" | \"boolean\"\n                        )\n                    {\n                        ty = Some(tt.to_string());\n                        break;\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Infer type if still missing\n            if ty.is_none() {\n                if map.contains_key(\"properties\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"required\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"additionalProperties\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"object\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"items\") || map.contains_key(\"prefixItems\") {\n                    ty = Some(\"array\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"enum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"const\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"format\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"string\".to_string());\n                } else if map.contains_key(\"minimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"maximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMinimum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"exclusiveMaximum\")\n                    || map.contains_key(\"multipleOf\")\n                {\n                    ty = Some(\"number\".to_string());\n                }\n            }\n            // If we still couldn't infer, default to string\n            let ty = ty.unwrap_or_else(|| \"string\".to_string());\n            map.insert(\"type\".to_string(), JsonValue::String(ty.to_string()));\n\n            // Ensure object schemas have properties map\n            if ty == \"object\" {\n                if !map.contains_key(\"properties\") {\n                    map.insert(\n                        \"properties\".to_string(),\n                        JsonValue::Object(serde_json::Map::new()),\n                    );\n                }\n                // If additionalProperties is an object schema, sanitize it too.\n                // Leave booleans as-is, since JSON Schema allows boolean here.\n                if let Some(ap) = map.get_mut(\"additionalProperties\") {\n                    let is_bool = matches!(ap, JsonValue::Bool(_));\n                    if !is_bool {\n                        sanitize_json_schema(ap);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Ensure array schemas have items\n            if ty == \"array\" &amp;&amp; !map.contains_key(\"items\") {\n                map.insert(\"items\".to_string(), json!({ \"type\": \"string\" }));\n            }\n        }\n        _ =&gt; {}\n    }\n}\n\n/// Builds the tool registry builder while collecting tool specs for later serialization.\npub(crate) fn build_specs(\n    config: &amp;ToolsConfig,\n    mcp_tools: Option&lt;HashMap&lt;String, mcp_types::Tool&gt;&gt;,\n) -&gt; ToolRegistryBuilder {\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ApplyPatchHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::GrepFilesHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ListDirHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::McpHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::McpResourceHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::PlanHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ReadFileHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ShellHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::TestSyncHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::UnifiedExecHandler;\n    use crate::tools::handlers::ViewImageHandler;\n    use std::sync::Arc;\n\n    let mut builder = ToolRegistryBuilder::new();\n\n    let shell_handler = Arc::new(ShellHandler);\n    let unified_exec_handler = Arc::new(UnifiedExecHandler);\n    let plan_handler = Arc::new(PlanHandler);\n    let apply_patch_handler = Arc::new(ApplyPatchHandler);\n    let view_image_handler = Arc::new(ViewImageHandler);\n    let mcp_handler = Arc::new(McpHandler);\n    let mcp_resource_handler = Arc::new(McpResourceHandler);\n\n    match &amp;config.shell_type {\n        ConfigShellToolType::Default =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(create_shell_tool());\n        }\n        ConfigShellToolType::Local =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::LocalShell {});\n        }\n        ConfigShellToolType::UnifiedExec =&gt; {\n            builder.push_spec(create_exec_command_tool());\n            builder.push_spec(create_write_stdin_tool());\n            builder.register_handler(\"exec_command\", unified_exec_handler.clone());\n            builder.register_handler(\"write_stdin\", unified_exec_handler);\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Always register shell aliases so older prompts remain compatible.\n    builder.register_handler(\"shell\", shell_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"container.exec\", shell_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"local_shell\", shell_handler);\n\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_mcp_resources_tool(), true);\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_mcp_resource_templates_tool(), true);\n    builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_read_mcp_resource_tool(), true);\n    builder.register_handler(\"list_mcp_resources\", mcp_resource_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"list_mcp_resource_templates\", mcp_resource_handler.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"read_mcp_resource\", mcp_resource_handler);\n\n    builder.push_spec(PLAN_TOOL.clone());\n    builder.register_handler(\"update_plan\", plan_handler);\n\n    if let Some(apply_patch_tool_type) = &amp;config.apply_patch_tool_type {\n        match apply_patch_tool_type {\n            ApplyPatchToolType::Freeform =&gt; {\n                builder.push_spec(create_apply_patch_freeform_tool());\n            }\n            ApplyPatchToolType::Function =&gt; {\n                builder.push_spec(create_apply_patch_json_tool());\n            }\n        }\n        builder.register_handler(\"apply_patch\", apply_patch_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"grep_files\".to_string())\n    {\n        let grep_files_handler = Arc::new(GrepFilesHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_grep_files_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"grep_files\", grep_files_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"read_file\".to_string())\n    {\n        let read_file_handler = Arc::new(ReadFileHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_read_file_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"read_file\", read_file_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .iter()\n        .any(|tool| tool == \"list_dir\")\n    {\n        let list_dir_handler = Arc::new(ListDirHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_list_dir_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"list_dir\", list_dir_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config\n        .experimental_supported_tools\n        .contains(&amp;\"test_sync_tool\".to_string())\n    {\n        let test_sync_handler = Arc::new(TestSyncHandler);\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_test_sync_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"test_sync_tool\", test_sync_handler);\n    }\n\n    if config.web_search_request {\n        builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::WebSearch {});\n    }\n\n    // Deep web search is now handled by MCP server\n    // if config.deep_web_search {\n    //     let deep_web_search_handler = Arc::new(crate::tools::handlers::DeepWebSearchHandler);\n    //     builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(\n    //         ToolSpec::Function(crate::tools::handlers::create_deep_web_search_tool()),\n    //         false, // Deep research is async and may take time\n    //     );\n    //     builder.register_handler(\"deep_web_search\", deep_web_search_handler);\n    // }\n\n    if config.include_view_image_tool {\n        builder.push_spec_with_parallel_support(create_view_image_tool(), true);\n        builder.register_handler(\"view_image\", view_image_handler);\n    }\n\n    if let Some(mcp_tools) = mcp_tools {\n        let mut entries: Vec&lt;(String, mcp_types::Tool)&gt; = mcp_tools.into_iter().collect();\n        entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&amp;b.0));\n\n        for (name, tool) in entries.into_iter() {\n            match mcp_tool_to_openai_tool(name.clone(), tool.clone()) {\n                Ok(converted_tool) =&gt; {\n                    builder.push_spec(ToolSpec::Function(converted_tool));\n                    builder.register_handler(name, mcp_handler.clone());\n                }\n                Err(e) =&gt; {\n                    tracing::error!(\"Failed to convert {name:?} MCP tool to OpenAI tool: {e:?}\");\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    builder\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use crate::client_common::tools::FreeformTool;\n    use crate::model_family::find_family_for_model;\n    use crate::tools::registry::ConfiguredToolSpec;\n    use mcp_types::ToolInputSchema;\n    use pretty_assertions::assert_eq;\n\n    use super::*;\n\n    fn tool_name(tool: &amp;ToolSpec) -&gt; &amp;str {\n        match tool {\n            ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool { name, .. }) =&gt; name,\n            ToolSpec::LocalShell {} =&gt; \"local_shell\",\n            ToolSpec::WebSearch {} =&gt; \"web_search\",\n            ToolSpec::Freeform(FreeformTool { name, .. }) =&gt; name,\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Avoid order-based assertions; compare via set containment instead.\n    fn assert_contains_tool_names(tools: &amp;[ConfiguredToolSpec], expected_subset: &amp;[&amp;str]) {\n        use std::collections::HashSet;\n        let mut names = HashSet::new();\n        let mut duplicates = Vec::new();\n        for name in tools.iter().map(|t| tool_name(&amp;t.spec)) {\n            if !names.insert(name) {\n                duplicates.push(name);\n            }\n        }\n        assert!(\n            duplicates.is_empty(),\n            \"duplicate tool entries detected: {duplicates:?}\"\n        );\n        for expected in expected_subset {\n            assert!(\n                names.contains(expected),\n                \"expected tool {expected} to be present; had: {names:?}\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn shell_tool_name(config: &amp;ToolsConfig) -&gt; Option&lt;&amp;'static str&gt; {\n        match config.shell_type {\n            ConfigShellToolType::Default =&gt; Some(\"shell\"),\n            ConfigShellToolType::Local =&gt; Some(\"local_shell\"),\n            ConfigShellToolType::UnifiedExec =&gt; None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn find_tool&lt;'a&gt;(\n        tools: &amp;'a [ConfiguredToolSpec],\n        expected_name: &amp;str,\n    ) -&gt; &amp;'a ConfiguredToolSpec {\n        tools\n            .iter()\n            .find(|tool| tool_name(&amp;tool.spec) == expected_name)\n            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(\"expected tool {expected_name}\"))\n    }\n\n    fn strip_descriptions_schema(schema: &amp;mut JsonSchema) {\n        match schema {\n            JsonSchema::Boolean { description }\n            | JsonSchema::String { description }\n            | JsonSchema::Number { description } =&gt; {\n                *description = None;\n            }\n            JsonSchema::Array { items, description } =&gt; {\n                strip_descriptions_schema(items);\n                *description = None;\n            }\n            JsonSchema::Object {\n                properties,\n                required: _,\n                additional_properties,\n            } =&gt; {\n                for v in properties.values_mut() {\n                    strip_descriptions_schema(v);\n                }\n                if let Some(AdditionalProperties::Schema(s)) = additional_properties {\n                    strip_descriptions_schema(s);\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn strip_descriptions_tool(spec: &amp;mut ToolSpec) {\n        match spec {\n            ToolSpec::Function(ResponsesApiTool { parameters, .. }) =&gt; {\n In Rust, cfg attributes apply at the item level, and I’m considering how tokens in disabled items may not be parsed. So, with `#[cfg(test)]`, this is an attribute on the module, which suggests the module item is parsed before applying cfg. However, I'm curious if tokens inside a cfg-disabled module are also parsed. **Exploring syntax errors and parsing in Rust**

I think syntax errors in cfg-disabled code aren't reported because the parser might not actually parse that code, even though tokenization recognizes certain structures like braces.
